# Evaluate a workflow change

Freeze the baseline, candidate, task briefs and rubric before generation. Use varied tasks covering initial drafting, review-only work, bounded rewriting, sparse evidence and voice preservation. Keep some tasks unseen during development and do not tune on the final test set.

Use separate fresh creator executions with the same model, effort, facts, number of attempts and output budget. Give each only its instructions and raw task materials. Keep synthetic samples clearly separate from actual user-approved examples.

Blind the reviewer to version identity, the author's rationale and any desired score. Vary candidate order. Score task fulfillment, supported specificity, argument, voice and preservation on a stated scale. Require concrete evidence for faults. An invented material fact or unauthorized action makes an output ineligible regardless of its stylistic score.

Report per-task results, ties and regressions; distinguish a fresh AI review from a user preference test. Keep generation and review artifacts with the evaluation record. If separate execution is unavailable, disclose that limitation; never describe a self-review as independent. Test demonstrated fixes on fresh cases before declaring improvement. A numerical target must not be given to the judge or substituted for user approval of the voice.

## Shared maintenance coordination

For a proposed persistent skill change, use `learning-loop` to connect this domain evaluation to the existing evidence ledger, candidate diff, promotion policy and recurrence monitoring. Retain this skill’s domain checks and normal task review; the maintenance experiment is not a new gate for ordinary deliverables. If the coordinator is unavailable, preserve the candidate and report the missing integration rather than claiming promotion.
